newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets fall.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets fall.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Wednesday that its international reserves were $21.446 billion as of May 2, compared with $21.718 billion on April 25.
The central bank said its net international assets as of the same date fell to $12.383 billion from $12.433 billion on April 25.
The central bank said the decline of $50 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net sales of foreign currency from the federal government worth $119 million.
--The purchase of $8.0 million from credit institutions, a product of the partial exercising of options on the sale of dollars to the central bank that were issued during the auction of April 15.
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $62 million.

--A net loss of $1.0 million due to a combination of factors, including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.

Banco de Mexico said that, in the same time frame, the monetary base rose 5.667 billion pesos due to a rise in the seasonal demand of bills and coins. In the same period, the government's balance at the central bank rose 3.191 billion pesos, due mainly to tax collections.

The bank said it undertook monetary regulation operations for a total of 9.237 billion pesos in the same period to meet greater demand for bills and coins, as well as to offset the increase in federal government deposits in the account it holds with the central bank.
The following tables details Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
May 2 Apr 25
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $21.446 bln $21.718 bln
Monetary Base 79.222 73.555
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $12.383 bln $12.433 bln
Net Domestic Credit -18.746 -24.564
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
